extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology containing metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: PDF files and metadata were crawled from the ACL Anthology, passed through full-text extraction, and enhanced using Semantic Scholar's API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology website.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files longer than 50 pages were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Published papers from online held CL conferences between 2020 and 2022 were crawled together with their topics from those websites to obtain ground truth topic labels.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID, PDFFigures, public language detection toolkit (Shuyo, 2010)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing newly added papers.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: It is a small-scale collection focusing only on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers, not a comprehensive corpus.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models, fine-tuning general LLMs, summarization, and related work generation.

name.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain.

description.evidence: Integrating and enhancing the previous versions of the ACL Anthology, the ACL OCL contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar).

url.evidence:
Our dataset is available from HuggingFace1.

inLanguage.evidence: English is the most dominant language processed in the ACL OCL. However, it is noteworthy that languages such as Latin and Gujarati are also present.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We start by crawling the PDF files and metadata from the source ACL Anthology. We then pass the PDF files through the full-text extraction process. We enhance this data using Semantic Scholar’s API to fetch additional information about OCL papers.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website... We use its Graph API8to connect an OCL document to its corresponding document in S2AG.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology published from 1952 to September 2022.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions4or handbooks.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We crawl published papers of several online held CL conferences (e.g., ACL 2020, EACL 2021) between 2020 and 2022, together with their topics from those websites. After aligning those papers with the data in the ACL OCL, we obtained 2545 documents classified in 21 topics in total

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we use GROBID7for the full-text extraction from PDF files... we extract figures and tables from PDF files using PDFFigures... To detect the language in which a document is written, we utilize a public language detection toolkit10 (Shuyo, 2010)

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: mainly because of the bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics (e.g., MT).

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: OCL aids tasks that demand complete textual content from scientific papers, such as document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models like Galactica (Taylor et al., 2022) or fine-tuning a general LLM like Llama
